front.title: Using the Well-Known IPv6 Prefix to Represent Non-Global IPv4 Addresses

abstract.t:
This document modifies the deployment guidance provided in Section 3.1 of RFC 6052 (IPv6 Addressing of IPv4/IPv6 Translators) that IPv4/IPv6 Translators must not use the Well-Known Prefix 64:ff9b::/96 to represent non-globally reachable IPv4 addresses, such as those defined in RFC 1918 (Address Allocation for Private Internets) or listed in Section 2.2.2 of RFC 6890 (Special-Purpose IP Address Registries). This change enables IPv6-only nodes to reach IPv4-only services with specific non-globally reachable addresses by leveraging the Well-Known Prefix.
This document updates RFC 6052 to allow packets in which an address is composed of the Well-Known Prefix and specific non-globally reachable IPv4 addresses to be translated.
